tasks.short: Collect source data, clean and convert it, run the spatial analysis, check the results, and document method and sources.

steps.what: GIS technician collects source data from portals and files
GIS technician performs geospatial data building by cleaning and converting the data
GIS technician performs spatial modelling and analysis
GIS technician checks the results for errors
GIS technician documents the method and data sources

tasks.design: Frequently used sources, such as national address, building and topography data, are connected as live services in the GIS ({OTHER}), so they are not downloaded and loaded by hand. Cleaning, conversion and standard analyses are saved as processing models that rerun on new data; about 60% of jobs reuse one, while new questions still need building by hand. Method and source notes are generated from the processing model. Checking results stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were downloaded and cleaned by hand for each job.
tasks.enabler_now: GIS tools connect to geodata services and save processing models.
tasks.still_hard: Client data come in odd formats and projections.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a result is spatially impossible.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks and builds new models instead of repeating steps.

evidence.claim: GIS tools can connect to geodata services and save processing models that rerun on new data.
Address data linked to people are personal data and need a lawful basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the analysis request to the method documented; presenting results is outside.
Input contract: services connected and models kept in a shared folder; fallback is downloads.
Scenario: about 60% of jobs reuse an existing processing model.
research_questions: Do repeat analyses come out faster and with fewer errors?

incremental.description: GIS technician maintains processing models when sources change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly new questions; high: mostly repeat analyses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather earlier requests and maps, meet the client, write notes and agreed specifications, check them, and send them to the client.

steps.what: GIS technician gathers the client's earlier requests and maps before the meeting
GIS technician meets with clients to discuss specifications, custom solutions or problems
GIS technician writes meeting notes and agreed specifications
GIS technician checks the final notes and specifications
GIS technician e-mails the notes and specifications to the client

tasks.design: Each client's requests, maps and specifications sit in one client page in the service desk ({HELPDESK}), so the technician does not search e-mails before a meeting. Notes are typed into a specification template with fields for data, scale, output and deadline during the meeting. Once checked, the notes go to the client from the client page. Meeting the client stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: History sat in e-mails and notes were written up afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Service desks keep requests and documents per client.
tasks.still_hard: Clients change specifications after the meeting.
tasks.human_edge: Finding out what the client really needs the map for.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk summarises tickets and keeps requests per caller.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting planned to notes sent; doing the work is outside.
Input contract: client requests logged in the service desk; fallback is e-mail.
The technician checks the notes before they go out.
research_questions: Do specification changes after meetings fall?

incremental.description: GIS technician files client documents on the client page.

approvals.approved_version: The notes and specifications as checked by the technician in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new clients with little history; high: regular clients with many requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide map content and symbology, style layers, lay out the map, export it in the needed formats, and check it.

steps.what: GIS technician decides map content and symbology
GIS technician prepares graphic representations of GIS data by styling layers by hand
GIS technician lays out the map with legend, scale and title
GIS technician exports maps in the needed formats and sizes
GIS technician checks the final maps

tasks.design: Saved layer styles and map layout templates in the organisation's house style ({OTHER}) cover the standard map types, about 70% of maps, so layers are styled and maps laid out from a template with legend, scale and title text filled in. Map series are exported in one batch in all formats. Deciding content and symbology and checking maps stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each map was styled and laid out by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: GIS tools save styles and layout templates and export map series in batch.
tasks.still_hard: Special maps for presentations need custom design.
tasks.human_edge: Making a busy map easy to read at a glance.

evidence.claim: GIS tools can save layer styles and layout templates and export map series in batch.

assumptions: Boundary: from the map request to maps checked; delivering maps is outside.
Input contract: house style templates kept by the GIS team; fallback is styling by hand.
Scenario: about 70% of maps are standard types covered by templates.
research_questions: Do maps look more consistent across the team?

incremental.description: GIS technician keeps style templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many custom presentation maps; high: mostly standard map series.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer users' GIS questions by e-mail and phone, help users at their screen, write how-to guides, and log support requests.

steps.what: GIS technician provides technical expertise by answering users' questions by e-mail and phone
GIS technician helps users at their screen
GIS technician writes how-to guides for common questions

loop.input: Resolved tickets on the same question and the technician's answer.
loop.output: A draft how-to guide with numbered steps.
loop.check: The technician tests every step in the GIS software and edits the guide before it is published.
loop.stop: One draft per guide; if rejected, the technician writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives the layout, not the steps for each question.

steps.what: GIS technician logs support requests in a list

tasks.design: Users ask GIS questions through a service desk form ({HELPDESK}), so requests are logged in the ticket instead of a separate list, and the form suggests matching how-to guides from the knowledge base, which answers some questions without the technician. Guides are drafted from resolved tickets and the technician tests and edits every step. Helping users at their screen stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions came by e-mail and phone and were logged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Service desks suggest knowledge items and draft them from tickets for review.
tasks.still_hard: Many questions are specific to one dataset.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a user is really trying to do with the map.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews guides instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk suggests category and priority, summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review.

assumptions: Boundary: from the user question to the request logged; training courses are outside.
Input contract: GIS questions routed through the service desk; fallback is e-mail.
The technician tests every guide before publishing.
Users read a suggested guide in about the time an e-mail took.
research_questions: Do repeat questions fall once guides exist?

already_counted.description: GIS technician tests and edits drafted guides.

incremental.description: Users read suggested guides before asking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly dataset-specific questions; high: many repeat how-to questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The GIS technician keeps checking analyses, deciding map design, meeting clients and helping users; hand downloads, manual styling, e-mail history and hand-written guides shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time on new analyses.

job.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
